subject: Hosted API: user-facing transparency copy + DPA/subprocessor link placement
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acmeanalytics.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2027-04-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask on privacy blurb for hosted API (public site)

Hi Camila —

We're finalizing our integration docs for the Acme Analytics data ingestion flow and want to include a short Redwood blurb about how you handle customer data for the hosted API. Our procurement/legal team asked whether the public-facing sentence can avoid listing subprocessors or any language that looks like a long legal disclosure. They prefer a concise, user-facing line that links to the full DPA/subprocessor list.

Current ask: can Redwood propose a 1–2 sentence consumer-facing blurb explaining: 1) what data you process in hosted API mode; 2) that subprocessors are used and a link to the full list. Prefer plain English.

Also, can you attach any simple diagram showing where customer data flows (we only need a high-level PNG)? That helps our security review.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ramos
Head of Integrations, Acme Analytics
From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on privacy blurb for hosted API (public site)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a draft DPA (redline v2) and a simple dataflow PNG for your security team. Below are two alternative public-facing blurbs — one verbatim-for-site and one shorter tooltip/dialog option. Please tell us which tone works for Acme.

Option A (site paragraph — ~2 sentences):
“Redwood Inference processes text and metadata you send to our Hosted API to perform model inference. We may engage subprocessors for storage and cloud infrastructure — view our full DPA and current subprocessor list here: [link to DPA & Subprocessors].”

Option B (short UI tooltip/button):
“We process data you send to our Hosted API. See our DPA and list of subprocessors for details.”

Karthik and Laura — tagging you for legal plain-language and regional phrasing review (especially 'subprocessors' vs 'third-party vendors').

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v2.docx (docx), dataflow-diagram.png (png)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-15T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on privacy blurb for hosted API (public site)

Thanks Camila — good starting points. A couple of editorial notes from the product/communications side:

1) 'Subprocessors' is accurate but not widely understood by non-legal readers. Recommend swapping to 'service providers' in consumer-facing copy, and keep 'subprocessors' in the DPA/legal page.
2) The first sentence should make clear what 'we' means (i.e., 'Redwood Inference'). Suggested edit for Option A:

“Redwood Inference processes the text and associated metadata you send to its Hosted API to generate model outputs. We may use third-party service providers to store and operate that data — see our DPA and current service provider list for details.”

3) For the tooltip (Option B) shorten to: “We process data you send to Redwood’s Hosted API. See our DPA & service provider list.”

Sofia — does Acme want a European copy variant (GDPR-friendly phrasing) or will the US copy be used as-is? If you need regional variants we can provide a one-line tweak.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Marketing, Redwood Inference
From: legal@acmeanalytics.com
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-15T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on privacy blurb for hosted API (public site)

Hi Camila / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments. A couple of notes from Acme Legal:

- We're fine with a shortened, user-facing line, but we need an explicit statement that customer content is not used to train models outside of a customer's environment (our procurement is sensitive here). Can you add a short parenthetical or second clause: e.g., 'We do not use customer content to train models for other customers.'

- For the 'service provider/subprocessor' term: we ask that the public copy uses the phrase 'service providers' as Laura suggested. The DPA can retain the term 'subprocessor.'

- Please confirm the subprocessor list link is stable (redirect to a hosted page) and that Redwood will notify customers of material changes. Procurement will require notification terms in the DPA itself — we flagged that in the redline.

Appreciate it — please send an updated blurb and we can move forward with embedding it in our docs.

—Acme Legal
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: legal@acmeanalytics.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on privacy blurb for hosted API (public site)

All — happy to reconcile. Proposed final public-facing line that addresses Acme Legal's training concern, uses 'service providers', and keeps the DPA link:

"Redwood Inference processes the text and metadata you send to its Hosted API to generate model outputs. We may use third-party service providers to store or operate that data; we do not use customer content to train models for other customers. See our DPA and current service provider list (link)."

Notes:
- We'll host the subprocessor/service provider list on a stable Redwood docs page and include a change-notice clause in the DPA (redline attached).
- If Acme wants a GDPR-specific variant, I can supply one-liners — e.g., swap 'we may use' with 'we may engage' and add 'where required by law or contractual commitments'.

Camila/Laura — if you're good with the phrasing I'll add it to the doc and send a clean copy for Acme to paste into their integration docs.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
